about: PWCC Marketplace was a Tigard, Oregon online marketplace and vault for collectible trading cards, including sports and Pokemon cards, offering auctions, instant offers and storage for collectors, and acting as a liquidity provider. Founded in 2000, it grew rapidly during the card boom. Fanatics Collectibles acquired it in 2022 and later rebranded it Fanatics Collect. Funding shown is about 175 million dollars. A well-known collector brand in the US.
cb_desc: Tangible asset marketplace, liquidity provider, and educat..

about: Casas Bahia, formally Grupo Casas Bahia, is one of Brazil's largest retailers of furniture, appliances and electronics, based in Sao Paulo, operating around 1,000 stores under the Casas Bahia and Ponto brands, plus its e-commerce platforms and a marketplace. It was formerly called Via, and was created by merging Via Varejo's brands and Casas Bahia, founded by Samuel Klein in 1952. It is listed on B3 as BHIA3 and has gone through financial restructuring. Funding shown is about 622 million reais. An extremely well-known Brazilian consumer retailer with a long record of TV advertising and sports sponsorship.

Hologic is a Marlborough, Massachusetts medical technology company known for women's health, with products in breast imaging (3D mammography), molecular diagnostics, surgical devices and Covid-19 testing. It sells to hospitals and labs globally, with revenue of about $4 billion. It was listed on Nasdaq (HOLX), and in 2025 agreed to be taken private by Blackstone and TPG in a deal valued at about $18 billion. B2B health brand with little general awareness.

SHINE Fusion is recorded by Crunchbase with a Melbourne, Australia location and a description of Shine Technologies as a digital consultancy, which does not match the name SHINE Fusion, a fusion-technology firm in the US, so the record is mixed. It is categorised under biotechnology and DevOps, with about $1.28 billion in funding and the latest round in August 2026. Which entity is meant, and its products and ownership, cannot be confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Exact Sciences is a Madison, Wisconsin diagnostics company known for Cologuard, a non-invasive stool-based colon cancer screening test, and Oncotype DX genomic tests for breast cancer, along with other cancer testing products. Customers are patients, physicians and health insurers, with revenue of more than 2 billion dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (EXAS). Crunchbase shows about 2.75 billion dollars of funding. Cologuard is widely advertised to US consumers aged 45 and over, so brand awareness is high.

Amicus Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in Princeton, New Jersey, and listed on Nasdaq (FOLD). It specialises in rare metabolic and lysosomal diseases, selling Galafold, an oral treatment for Fabry disease, and Pombiliti plus Opfolda, a combination therapy for late-onset Pompe disease. Customers are specialist physicians, hospitals and patients in the US, Europe, Japan and other markets. Revenue is roughly $500 million to $600 million a year, with total funding of about $2.6 billion. Known mainly to rare-disease doctors and investors, with no consumer brand awareness.

US software company that sells revenue management cloud software to life sciences and technology manufacturers, helping them manage pricing, rebates, contracts and compliance, with customers including pharmaceutical and medical device firms. Revenue comes from subscriptions and services. It was listed on the NYSE (MODN) and taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2021 for about 1.25 billion dollars. B2B, with a strong reputation among pharma commercial teams, and no consumer awareness.

Chinese cell therapy company developing CAR-T treatments, including zevor-cel (zevorcabtagene) for multiple myeloma, approved in China, and satri-cel (CT041) targeting Claudin 18.2 in gastric cancer. Listed on the Hong Kong exchange (2171). Customers are hospitals. Revenue is early. Specialist oncology company with no consumer brand. Founded in 2014, it also has manufacturing facilities in Shanghai and Durham, North Carolina, supporting studies in China and the US.

emeis (formerly Orpea) is a Puteaux, France operator of nursing homes, rehabilitation and psychiatric clinics and home care, with around 1,000 facilities in over 20 countries and about 70,000 employees. It restructured after the 2022 Orpea scandal and renamed to emeis in 2023, with the state-backed Caisse des Depots among its shareholders. Listed on Euronext Paris (EMEIS). A care brand, relevant mainly to families, with a reputational challenge for sponsorship.

Owens & Minor is a Glen Allen, Virginia-based healthcare logistics company, listed on the NYSE (OMI), distributing medical and surgical supplies to hospitals and manufacturing medical products (Halyard). It also has home health business Apria. Revenue is about $10 billion. B2B with strong healthcare industry recognition and little consumer branding.

Fakeeh.Care is the healthcare group built around the Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, a leading private hospital founded in 1978 that offers internal medicine, urology, ENT, emergency and many other specialties. It has expanded with hospitals in Dubai and Riyadh and a university and nursing college. Customers are patients and insurers. A well known private healthcare brand in Saudi Arabia, a F1 host country.
cb_desc: Fakeeh.Care specializes in internal medicine, urology, EN..

about: Aster DM Healthcare is a healthcare group founded by Dr Azad Moopen in 1987, headquartered in Dubai. It operates hospitals, clinics and retail pharmacies across the GCC under Aster, Medcare and Access brands, and in India through Aster hospitals, serving patients and insurers. Its structure was split between a Gulf business and an Indian business, listed on the NSE and BSE as Aster DM Healthcare. Revenue is over $1 billion. Familiar healthcare brand in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Kerala, with limited global profile.

Olam Agri is the food, feed and fibre business of Olam Group, based in Singapore, trading and processing grains, rice, edible oils, flour and cotton, and selling packaged staple foods to consumers in Africa. Saudi Arabia's SALIC bought a major stake (about 44 percent) in 2022. Customers are food manufacturers, farmers and consumers across emerging markets. Strong staple food brands in Africa, but little visibility in the main F1 markets.
cb_desc: Olam Agri offers food, feed and fibre in high-growth emerging....

about: Madison Air is a Chicago-based industrial technology company, owned by Madison Industries, making air-quality, heating, ventilation and air-handling products for commercial, industrial and data-centre customers, with businesses such as Mestek, Air Innovations and Dyna-Air. It reported funding of about 2.25 billion dollars and has been reported as preparing a stock market listing. Customers are builders, HVAC contractors and industrial operators. B2B manufacturer with limited consumer profile.

Olam International is a Singapore-based agri-business and food ingredients group, founded in 1989, trading and processing cocoa, coffee, cashews, spices, dairy, edible nuts, cotton and grains. Since 2022 it has operated through Olam Food Ingredients (ofi) and Olam Agri, with Saudi Arabia's SALIC buying a majority of Olam Agri. Customers are food, beverage and consumer goods manufacturers in around 60 countries, with revenue above $40 billion. Temasek's Aranda is the largest shareholder and the shares are listed on the SGX. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Olam International
wiki.what: Nigerian agriculture company listed in SGX
wiki.text: Olam International is a Nigerian-founded agri-business company, operating in 60 countries and supplying food and industrial raw materials to over 20,900 customers worldwide, placing them among the world's largest suppliers of cocoa beans, coffee, cotton and rice. Its value chain includes farming, origination, processing and distribution operations, child labor, and allegedly even child slavery.

about: Corteva Agriscience is a US agricultural company based in Indianapolis, created in 2019 when DowDuPont split its agriculture arm. It sells corn and soybean seeds under the Pioneer and Brevant brands, and crop protection products such as herbicides, insecticides and biologicals, to farmers and distributors in over 140 countries. Revenue is around $16-17 billion. Listed on the NYSE under CTVA, and in 2025 it announced plans to separate its seed and crop protection businesses. Strong brand with farmers, almost no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Corteva
wiki.text: Corteva, Inc. (also known as Corteva Agriscience) is an American company devoted to products for seeds and crop protection, including herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and biologicals (natural herbicides) that are sold in 110 countries. The company's name combines "cor" (Latin for "heart") with "teva" (the Hebrew word for nature). It is headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Its primary brand is Pioneer Hi-Bred International.

about: Trans-Oil Group of Companies is a Geneva-registered agribusiness whose main operations are in Moldova, one of the country's largest groups, in sunflower oil, grain, soy, other oilseeds, storage and export, with farming land and an oil extraction and trading business serving customers in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. It is privately held. Crunchbase shows about $1.2 billion in funding, with the latest round in June 2026. B2B commodity brand, with limited consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Trans-Oil Group of Companies deals in vegetable oil, oilseeds...

about: Indorama Fertilizers, commonly Indorama Eleme Fertilizer and Chemicals, is a Nigerian fertiliser producer based in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, part of the Indorama Group, operating the largest urea fertiliser plant in sub-Saharan Africa from its Eleme complex. It sells urea for farming, chemicals and exports. The wider group is based in Singapore. Crunchbase shows about 1.7 billion dollars of funding in 2026. B2B agricultural and chemicals brand with strong recognition in Nigerian farming and industry.

Indigo Ag is a Boston-based agricultural technology company that sells biological seed treatments and runs a carbon market programme paying farmers for storing carbon in soil, as well as a grain marketplace and sustainability services. Customers are farmers and food and ingredient buyers. Venture-backed and once valued above three billion dollars, it has since scaled back and restructured. Crunchbase shows about 1.44 billion dollars of funding. B2B agtech brand with moderate recognition among US farmers.

Inari is a US agricultural biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2016 and backed by Flagship Pioneering. It uses gene editing and data science to design seeds with higher yields and lower input needs, starting with soybeans and corn, and plans to license or sell seed to farmers through partners and seed distributors. It is privately held and has raised around $750 million. B2B seed technology firm with little public brand awareness.
cb_desc: Inaris a seed design and biotechnology company...

about: ProducePay is a Los Angeles agricultural technology and fintech company that provides financing, logistics and market access to produce growers in Latin America and the US, advancing payments for crops and connecting them to buyers. Customers are farmers and fresh produce buyers such as retailers and distributors. It is a B2B firm with little consumer visibility. Founded in 2014, it operates across the Americas and is private and venture-backed.

German agricultural and construction trading group, based in Munich, trading grain, fertiliser and farm machinery, supplying building materials through BayWa Baustoffe, and running the renewable energy developer BayWa r.e. It serves farmers, builders and utilities in Germany, Austria and abroad, and employs about 20,000 people. Owned by a cooperative, it faced a financial crisis in 2023 and 2024 and underwent a restructuring with lenders. Well known to German farmers and tradespeople.

Ardagh Metal Packaging is a Luxembourg-based supplier of metal beverage cans, producing aluminium and steel cans for beer, soft drinks, energy drinks and other beverages from plants in Europe and the Americas, for customers such as Coca-Cola, Heineken, PepsiCo and Carlsberg. Revenue is about 5 billion dollars. It listed on the NYSE (AMBP) in 2021 after a SPAC merger, and is majority owned by Ardagh Group. B2B packaging brand with no consumer awareness, though its cans reach consumers widely.

Boliden is a Swedish metals company that mines and smelts copper, zinc, lead, gold and silver, with mines in Sweden, Finland, Norway and Ireland and smelters in Sweden, Finland and Norway, and produces recycled metals. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, with about 6,000 employees and revenue of about 80 billion kronor. Customers are industrial metal buyers and traders. Headquartered in Stockholm. B2B commodity supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

American Water Works (American Water) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility in the US by population served, based in Camden, New Jersey and listed on the NYSE (AWK). It supplies water and wastewater services to around 14 million people in about 14 states, plus military-base services. Revenue is regulated utility rates, about $4 billion a year. Utility with strong local recognition but little consumer brand marketing.

Emirates Central Cooling Systems Corporation, known as Empower, is Dubai's district cooling provider, with the world's largest district cooling company by connected capacity. It supplies chilled water to buildings in areas such as Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and Dubai Marina, and is mainly owned by Dubai Investments with a public listing on the Dubai Financial Market (EMPOWER). Customers are developers and building owners. Essential utility, B2B in nature with limited consumer brand awareness.
